title: Father of All, Omniscient Mind
description: Father of All, Omniscient Mind in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Blacklock wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 111 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Omniscience and Omnipresence”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther of all, om-ni-scient Mind, Thy wis-dom who can com-pre-hend? Its high-est point what eye can find, Or to its low-est depths de-scend?

lines: Father of all, omniscient Mind,
Thy wisdom who can comprehend?
Its highest point what eye can find,
Or to its lowest depths descend?
If up to heaven's ethereal height,
Thy prospect to elude, I rise,
In splendor there supremely bright,
Thy presence shall my sight surprise.
Thee, mighty God, my wondering soul,
Thee, all her conscious powers adore,
Whose being circumscribes the whole,
Whose eyes the universe explore.
Thine essence fills this breathing frame;
It glows in every vital part,
Lights up our souls with livelier flame,
And feeds with life each beating heart.
To thee, from whom our being came,
Whose smile is all the heaven we know,
Inspired with this exalted theme,
To thee our grateful strains shall flow.

licence: Public domain: Thomas Blacklock died in 1791.
credits: Words by Thomas Blacklock (1721–1791), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
